pull.title: wallet, rpc, gui: Allow users to manually rebroadcast a wallet transaction
pull.body: From the discussion in #36403, it is clear that there needs to be a way for users to rebroadcast a transaction. Currently, the way to do so requires getting the raw transaction, getting the hex, and using `sendrawtransaction`. This PR adds `rebroadcastwallettx` RPC that takes a txid to attempt to rebroadcast that single transaction. An action is also added to the GUI menu for each transaction to do the same.

Concept ACK

Whatever the solution of the existing issues with rebroadcast will be, giving the users the option to rebroadcast transactions manually is useful in all of these scenarios.

Concept ACK

One issue should be fixed before merge: `rebroadcastwallettx` fails with code -1 and an empty message when the transaction is out of the mempool and its feerate is above the wallet's `-maxfeerate`.

I ran the RPC on regtest at 648450039a. Other mempool rejections keep their reason, such as "bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent" for a child whose parent expired. The empty message shows up when a user lowers `-maxfeerate` to 20 sat/vB and restarts without mempool.dat. Our own 50 sat/vB child of an incoming payment then stays out of the mempool, and the RPC returns `{"code": -1, "message": ""}`. For the same transaction, `sendrawtransaction` with `maxfeerate=0.0002` returns -25 "Fee rate exceeds maximum configured by user (maxfeerate)".

The cause is that `Chain::broadcastTransaction` returns only a bool, and `BroadcastTransaction` sets no error string for `MAX_FEE_EXCEEDED` or `MAX_FEE_RATE_EXCEEDED`. `sendrawtransaction` falls back to `TransactionErrorString` in that case. The wallet's other callers only log the string or drop it, so this RPC is the first to show it to a user. The same fallback inside the `Chain::broadcastTransaction` wrapper would fix it, and the GUI action will need that message once it shows the result. I can share the probe script.

This will need a release note.

Also might be worth taking a look at ralph comments, specially the GUI crash, the blocks sync and the empty error messages :)

In commit "gui: Add rebroadcast tx menu action" (96c0e432770d5396294034618d35260510211bff)

Could this (and `RebroadcastSingleTransaction`) return `util::Result<void>` instead of `util::Expected<void, wallet::WalletError>`? That would make the interface say what it returns: an error message, with no codes callers are expected to handle.

`WalletError` can hold any of six codes, but this method only returns two, `InvalidParameter` and `MiscError`, and callers can't tell that from the declaration. None of them handles the codes differently either: the GUI shows the message, and the RPC only uses the code to pick an RPC error number. The `WalletErrorCode` documentation asks for a specific code only "when callers need to handle the condition differently", and `GenericError` otherwise (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/0e38ad26af922abdc0fc36c9379e17efd2a72b80/src/wallet/types.h#L63-L65).

`util::Result` is meant for this case, functions reporting error strings to end users, and `displayAddress()` above already returns `util::Result<void>`. `TransactionCanBeBroadcast` could return it too, instead of `util::Expected<void, bilingual_str>`. The RPC could then throw `RPC_WALLET_ERROR` for failures. It would also stop "Wallet broadcast is disabled" from being reported as an invalid parameter. If the RPC should report an unknown txid the way `gettransaction` does (`RPC_INVALID_ADDRESS_OR_KEY`), it could check `mapWallet` itself before calling, without a wallet-wide code. Since `rebroadcastwallettx` is new, no client depends on its error codes yet.

Using `util::Expected<void, bilingual_str>` instead of `util::Result<void>` would be fine too. My main concern is the signature saying the function can return error codes that it never returns and no caller handles.

My understanding is that for the QML GUI, they generally want error codes as some errors may be handled differently. While the GUI as I have implemented it currently does not use these codes, that does not preclude the future GUI work from using them either, and I'd prefer to avoid needing another interface change at that time as well. cc @pseudoramdom 

Even for the new RPC, I think it makes sense to get the codes so that we can give reasonable RPC error codes. I think it is incorrect to return RPC_WALLET_ERROR for things that are clearly the user providing a transaction that cannot be broadcast, hence using InvalidParameter so that it can return RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER.

Furthermore, I agree that it is strange that "Wallet broadcast is disabled" is InvalidParameter, but I don't think the solution is to drop the error codes from the wallet, but rather that `TransactionCanBeBroadcast` should use `util::Expected<void, WalletError>` as well, which I've done.

> Why not use `wtx.isBlockConflicted()`?

This is moved code.

> Also random and unrelated question. Why `IsUnconfirmed()` checks if there is any mempool conflict? That existance of a mempool conflict doesn't change the unconfirmed state...

Same reason it checks `isAbandoned()` and `isConflicted` - unconfirmed in this context means that this transaction is unconfirmed, and we want/expect it to become confirmed. If the transaction is abandoned or has a conflict already in the mempool, we either do not want it to become confirmed, or it cannot become confirmed.
